subject: Energy
title: Water and Energy
description: A quick, practical guide to Water and Energy.

hook.text: Energy production is the second-largest user of water globally—power plants need vast amounts for cooling.

buildup.text: Thermal plants (coal, gas, nuclear) boil water for steam—then need cooling water to condense it back in a loop.

discovery.text: A typical coal plant uses 2 billion liters of water per year—enough to supply a small city.

twist.text: Solar PV and wind use virtually no water—a major advantage in drought-prone regions facing water scarcity.

climax.text: Climate change worsens the nexus—droughts reduce hydropower and force thermal plants to shut down without cooling.

punchline.text: Power needs water, water needs power—the energy-water nexus.

quiz.question: Which energy sources use the least water?
